findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed member of staff to not use a barrier when turning off faucet after hand washing. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and hands were rewashed. Ensure a barrier is used after hand washing to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed a bag of sugar to be stored in a container of opened raisins. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper food storage. Raisins were discarded and bag of sugar will no longer be stored with raisins. Ensure food items a re stored in a way that prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-306.11 Food Display. Except for nuts in the shell and whole, raw fruits and vegetables that are intended for hulling, peeling, or washing by the CONSUMER before consumption, FOOD on display shall be protected from contamination by the use of PACKAGING; counter, service line, or salad bar FOOD guards; display cases; or other effective means.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed four dented enchilada cans on the shelves in the dry storage. PIC was made aware. The dented cans were immediately removed and store in a different location. Ensure that dented cans or packaged food items maintain their sealing integrity at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The internal surface of the coffee maker was observed soiled. PIC was made aware. The coffee maker was cleaned and sanitized while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the internal surface of the coffee maker are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The shelvings in the dish room use to store dishes were observed to be rusted. Discussed with PIC. PIC told inspector that the necessary actions will be taken. Ensure that the shelvings are cleaned and painted with anti-rust paint to cover the current surface.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The caulking on the left counter top of the dish machine was observed in disrepair. PIC was made aware. The counter top was re-caulked while inspector was present. Ensure sealed spaces remain sealed providing smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the CFPMs in the facility to not have allergen trainings. Discussed with PIC and PIC indicated that they are working on enrolling all kitchen employees in the allergen training class. Ensure at least one CFPM on staff at any given time of operation has the allergen awareness training.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P)

Upon arrival to inspection, 5-gal bucket of chlorine sanitizer observed empty. Staff replaced the bucket for a new one. Facility does not have test strips for chlorine (see #48). PIC placed call to Ecolab to order new chlorine strips. In the meantime, facility opted to switch from chlorine to quaternary ammonium sanitizer so they are able to test it and verify it is sanitizing. Inspector re-primed machine with quat sanitizer and strips yielded a concentration of 400ppm. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Facility does not have test strips for chlorine sanitizing dish machine, chlorine was the in-use sanitizer upon inspector arrival. See #16. Facility opted to use quaternary ammonium sanitizer until test strips can be ordered. 

Discussed sanitizing procedures with present staff. Test strips must be on hand at all times for working containers of sanitizers to ensure the concentration is sufficient enough to destroy pathogens. Although the container may be full, a blockage in the lines (for example) could prevent sanitizer from making it onto equipment to be sanitized. Testing the concentration at least once daily via a test strip is the only way to verify sanitizing step is working. 

Follow up issued for test strips. Text/call inspector when received chlorine test strips from Ecolab.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Observed employee go from handling dirty dishes, to quickly rinsing fingertips in handsink, to handling clean dishes two times. Inspector asked employee to properly wash hands for 20 seconds with soap, water, and paper towels to dry hands (using paper towels to shut off faucet once done drying hands). Education provided. Ensure all employees follow this procedure at all times. Additional education provided to PIC at time of inspection.

*Ensure online course is an ANSI accredited program.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Food employee was observed touching the manual faucet with her hands to shut off the water prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Hands were properly washed prior to continuing on to the next task. An educational handout showing proper technique was provided, and kitchen manager was advised to discuss handwashing with all staff. 

To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(E)(4) The baffle and ceiling inside the ice machine behind the baffle were soiled with mold. Cleaning frequency was discussed with kitchen manager.
 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. Clean and sanitize all components of the ice machine as needed.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 A package of roast beef deli meat was observed with a date mark of 1/2/19 in the walkin cooler. Manager stated that was the day the product was originally opened and frozen. The deli meat was pulled from the freezer yesterday and would be used today. Proper date marking was discussed. Kitchen manager was advised to make sure the date is being marked accordingly when foods are frozen and then changed when products are removed from the freezer for thawing to accurately represent the time frame by which foods are to be used or discarded.  

Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly marked, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer solution prepared using the wall mounted dispenser. Only a chlorine test kit was available, and none of the products used in the food service area have an active chlorine ingredient. Manager ordered test strips during the inspection and noted they would arrive with an order next week. Inspector provided some test strips for use until the new strips just ordered today are available for use.

A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided. Obtain and use quat test strips with sanitizer used on food contact surfaces in the kitchen.
